rapport_notes: Rep struggled with customer's hearing difficulty and communication clarity throughout; minimal warmth or reassurance offered despite customer's repeated requests for clarity and email confirmation.
process_discipline_notes: Rep did not hold silence after the estimate delivery—immediately offered clarification on the arrival window without pause for customer processing.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches into logistics questions ('What is the weight of the table?') without any framing, time-boxed ask, or promise of accurate quote.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight to fact-gathering about the table specs and delivery logistics.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep probed into table weight/materials, dimensions, assembly requirements, pallet situation, and HOA notification needs—multiple follow-ups on customer's stated concerns about the table's fragility and delivery complexity.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Implied in rep's statement: 'I just need to coordinate with our manager to see if we can safely move this knowing that it's a £250 and very Rashi'—acknowledges care/safety concern.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Not addressed. Rep never mentions who the specific movers are, crew lead, or any personalization of the team.
evidence_quotes.communication_covered: Rep offers email communication: 'Yes, ma'am. I can send you an email' and 'I'll just send you an email and then just let us know through email on what would be the best time for you.'
evidence_quotes.estimate: Rep gives a minimum-hour anchor: 'we do have a minimum hour of two and a half and we will be sending you two movers for this move. So basically ma'am for the two and a half hour, that's $550.' Does personalize by mentioning two movers, but no typical-range framing ('a typical [size] takes [N] movers [X–Y] hours').
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: None of the five lines appear. No commitment framing, no 'estimate is a window' language with specific factors, no 'beats it pay less' offer, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' + silence.
evidence_quotes.close: Rep ends with 'Alright, thank you so much for your time ma'am' and 'You're very welcome. Enjoy the rest of your day, bye-bye.'—no rate-lock language, no explicit ask for the booking.

top_strength: Rep stayed patient and probing through a complex, detailed scenario involving a fragile stone table, pallet removal, elevator logistics, and HOA coordination, drilling down multiple times to clarify specs and build an accurate picture of the job.
coaching_note: Completely skip the discovery framing (quid pro quo) and the customer's agenda question—these are non-negotiable first steps; jump straight into the differentiators (damage/carefulness, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, Communication) based on what the customer actually cares about, and close with a clear rate-lock and booking ask.
